classes.title: A state is reachable by construction but its exit was never implemented
classes.mechanism: Reachability and exit are authored in different artifacts and nobody enumerates their product. An enum member is selectable in the console, an outcome enum is persisted by a writer, a catch block renders an error branch, a fallback component mounts — and the corresponding exit (executor that sets executedAt, generation branch, retry affordance, consumer route for an emitted URL, control matching the imperative in the copy) lives in a different file that was never joined to it. The row is structurally valid, the screen renders, nothing throws; the user or the sweep simply has nowhere to go. Each round closes one cell and the neighbouring cell reappears at the same line with a different enum value.
exemplars: coachflow#1 apps/api/src/modules/booking/booking-lifecycle.service.ts — ACCOUNT_CREDIT then PACKAGE_CREDIT recorded with executedAt null; sweep ignores both forever
coachflow#1 apps/api/src/modules/booking/booking.service.ts — SEMI_PRIVATE slot is selectable and routed but the guard 400s every non-PRIVATE request
coachflow#4 apps/api/src/modules/auth/google/google-oauth.service.ts — COACH_STAFF with no memberships falls to '/', which the console layout bounces to /login

luxebook#109 apps/booking/src/app/[locale]/[tenantSlug]/tenant-unavailable-view.tsx — recovered tenant + 503 services seeds an empty list and tells the customer the salon has no services, with no retry
luxebook#1 apps/console/app/(console)/payments/page.tsx — copy directs coaches to a credit-note correction only the Stripe refund webhook can trigger
nutribuddy#113 tests/unit/desktop-discover.test.ts — state table stops at ready; creating-recipe and recipe-error states required by the handoff have no implementation or contract
classes.why_it_did_not_fire: trigger keywords too narrow — the rule fires on `status !== 'X'` predicates in backend guards, so it audits which values a GUARD admits, never whether each admitted value has a downstream executor, UI control, or route. The exits live in sweeps, TSX, and notification templates that the trigger never reaches.
classes.gate_idea: Reflect the enum out of schema.prisma / the TS union and generate the cartesian product (outcome × funding-mode × visibility × payment-method). For each cell run create → list → fulfil → view and assert the row reaches a terminal executed state or the write is rejected at creation; a cell ending with executedAt === null after the sweep drains fails. Unimplemented cells must be listed in a committed UNSUPPORTED_VARIANTS file the spec reads, so holes are visible in review rather than latent. Pair with a reachability probe: grep every URL template emitted by notification templates and every pdfUrl/download key in API projections and assert each resolves to a registered route with a matching method; and a lint pairing user-facing strings containing an imperative ('sign in with another account', 'issue a credit note') with a rendered control or handler in the same subtree.
classes.implementer_question: For every enum member and error branch this diff makes reachable, name the file:line of the thing that gets the user or the row OUT of it — the executor that stamps executedAt, the route that consumes the URL you emit, the retry control in the same subtree as the failure copy. Which cell of the matrix has a writer but no exit?

classes.title: A name is encoded twice with different resolution mechanisms
classes.mechanism: Producer and consumer each independently encode what a name refers to, and nothing forces them to agree — because the two sides resolve it through different machinery. vercel.json uses @secret syntax while the runbook creates Project Settings vars; Compose interpolates ${VAR} before service env_file applies; a volume key resolves to a different prefixed name under a second compose file with the same project; metadata-action publishes 7-char sha tags while the deploy input takes full sha-<commit>; env.schema hard-requires a key deploy.yml never passes with -e; a client is repointed cross-origin while the CORS allowlist and cookie Domain still assume same-origin; hostnames, base paths, media hosts and proxy-trust are literals in app code while the real topology lives in nginx and next.config.js. Every instance reads identically to a human and resolves to a different object at runtime — including one that silently boots Postgres on an empty volume.
exemplars: coachflow#7 infra/ec2-compose-interim.yml — same project name makes the interim key resolve to coachflow_pgdata and the target key to coachflow_coachflow_pg; cutover boots an empty database
coachflow#2 .github/workflows/api-image.yml — type=sha defaults to 7-char tags, deploy input takes full sha-<commit>, compose pull fails
luxebook#85 apps/api/src/config/env.schema.ts — CUSTOMER_CONTACT_HASH_SECRET hard-required in production but never passed into the container; next deploy exits during validateEnv
luxebook#88 apps/booking/src/lib/runtime-config.ts — API sets the manage-session cookie with no Domain, so the page on the apex origin cannot read it and recovered customers bounce
luxebook#78 apps/api/src/modules/booking/booking.service.ts — BOOKING_URL unset falls back to a hardcoded vercel.app host and still mints tokenized magic links to a foreign domain
nutribuddy config — placeholder D1 database IDs and per-environment Wrangler bindings shipped unvalidated; the binding the route reads is not the one the env declares
classes.why_it_did_not_fire: trigger keywords too narrow — the rule is keyed on `env.schema`, `deploy.yml`, `secrets.X`, so it fires only for environment VARIABLES. Volume keys, image tags, bind-mount sources, cookie Domain, CORS origin lists, basePath and registry identities are the same mechanism but match no trigger. And where it did fire, four-consumer counts how MANY consumers read a name, never whether producer and consumer resolve it through the same mechanism (shell env vs compose interpolation vs @secret vs build ARG).
classes.gate_idea: One repo-wide contract script in CI: (1) parse vercel.json, compose files, workflows and runbook fenced commands for every referenced name and grep app source for readers — fail on any name with zero readers or any reader with zero writers; (2) `docker compose -f A config` vs `-f B config` and diff resolved volume names, image refs and bind sources, failing on any key that resolves differently; (3) resolve every bind `source:` against the git index and fail on untracked paths; (4) every production-required key in env.schema.ts must appear as `-e KEY=` in deploy.yml AND in docker-compose.production.yml; (5) fail on any `https?://` literal in apps/api/src outside an allowlist, and assert every path prefix the API hands to clients (/uploads, /media, /api) has a matching proxy rule or rewrite in each frontend.
classes.implementer_question: For every name this diff introduces or renames — env key, volume, image tag, bind path, secret reference, cookie Domain, CORS origin — cite the exact file:line on the CONSUMING side that reads it, and confirm the resolution mechanism is the same one the producer used. Does `docker compose -f interim config` and `-f target config` resolve your volume key to the same string?

classes.title: A domain rule is enforced per call site, so new values and new writers escape it
classes.mechanism: An enum member, an authoritative field, or a business gate is duplicated across guards, `in:`/`notIn:` literals, badge maps, report filters and operator entry points instead of being carried by an exhaustive type or by the transition itself. Two failure directions, same root: a new status is written by one path while sibling guards, occupancy predicates, collection lists and UI mappers keep their old value set; and a new operator/bulk endpoint performs a transition with its own inline `update` while the canonical method's side effects (policy rows, counters, reminder cleanup, notifications) stay in the caller it bypassed. Nothing fails to compile because the old set is a valid subset and the old column still exists — the numbers just quietly disagree between screens and rows land in states no consumer handles.

luxebook#79 apps/api/src/modules/booking/booking.service.ts — applyLateDecision CANCEL flips status only, never writing cancellationOutcomeStatus or incrementing noShowCount the way cancelBooking/markNoShow do

coachflow#1 apps/api/src/modules/booking/booking.service.ts — booking lookup scopes by id/business only, so a known sessionId sells seats on a DRAFT/HIDDEN offering

nutribuddy — right-swipe recording does not re-check card safety that the card renderer already enforces

Ban inline status arrays in query `where` clauses for money/inventory models — require importing a named set from a single status-sets.ts. If you wrote a new `prisma.booking.update` reaching a status an existing service method already reaches, why did you not call that method — and where do you reproduce its counter increments and reminder cleanup?

classes.title: The error path commits, acks, or terminalizes without knowing which failure occurred
classes.mechanism: An operation mutates a primary row plus at least one other store (object storage, cache, second table, remote provider, reminder rows) with no single unit of commit, and the catch block then makes a durability decision the error does not justify. Swallow-and-ack: a dependent step fails, the webhook is still marked completed, so the provider never redelivers and no retry source remains. Terminalize-the-ambiguous: a transport timeout — where the external effect MAY have happened — is recorded as a definite rejection, so the retry moves money twice. Structural variants: `set -e` aborts the script before the rollback it was written to invoke; `process.exit(1)` bypasses cleanup leaving a live trial subscription; an artifact is uploaded before the DB write with no compensating delete; PostHog/email/reminder calls run through the root client inside a serializable callback so they survive an abort; a catch-all `@Catch()` or a shared transaction helper maps an entire failure space onto one domain-specific message.
exemplars: coachflow#1 apps/api/src/modules/payments/connect/refunds.service.ts — a network timeout after Stripe created the refund marks the row FAILED; the retry mints a new key and issues a second real refund
coachflow#1 apps/api/src/modules/payments/connect/connect-webhook.service.ts — catch swallows a transient fetch failure and the event still takes the completedAt path, so Stripe will not redeliver

luxebook#94 apps/api/src/common/telemetry/booking-event-bridge.ts — emitAsync awaited inside the serializable transaction, so booking_created flushes for a transaction that later aborts

classes.why_it_did_not_fire: the gate existed but asserted the wrong thing — the rule reasons about which LAYER owns rollback inside a transaction, and is satisfied by a correctly-layered tx. It has no notion of classifying a caught error as terminal vs ambiguous, no notion of a compensating delete for an artifact created before the write, and no reach at all into shell scripts where `set -e` is the thing that skips the compensation.
classes.gate_idea: Lint: in webhook/payment directories, a `catch` whose body does not rethrow, write a row selected by a named sweep query, or carry an `// AMBIGUOUS-SAFE:` annotation is an error; forbid non-`tx` clients (this.prisma, storage, notificationService, emitAsync) inside any `$transaction` callback; forbid mutating arrays declared outside the callback from inside it. For shell: under `set -e`, any `systemctl restart|start`, `tee` into /etc/systemd, or `docker run` must be followed by `|| { rollback; exit 1; }` or be preceded by a `trap ... ERR`. Back both with fault injection: wrap the provider client and inject {terminal-rejection, timeout-after-success, timeout-before-send} at each mutating call site, asserting 'provider effect count === 1' after replaying to completion; and a chaos job that runs the deploy step with a deliberately invalid drop-in and asserts the unit-file set is byte-identical and the service is active at exit.
classes.implementer_question: For every catch and every early exit this diff adds around an external call: list the mutations already committed at that point (remote resources, uploaded objects, cookies, holds, rows) and name the compensating action. After this catch runs, what is the concrete retry source — provider redelivery, a persisted job row, or a sweep query that still selects this row? And if the error was a timeout rather than a rejection, is the effect count still exactly one?

classes.title: The probe asserts something adjacent to the claim, so it can only produce false PASS
classes.mechanism: A gate, probe, or test is written to produce a green signal about X but inspects X' — a cheap proxy for the property customers experience, or an artifact of the implementation rather than the behavior. `systemctl is-active` passes while the connector is deregistered; a 200 status line is read while `|| true` discards a transfer error on a stalled body; `curl -k` accepts any certificate; a contract probe greps for a string that occurs in a DIFFERENT request in the same file, so the assertion is satisfied by an unrelated match; a smoke test SKIPS when a precondition is unmet and reports green; an expectation is computed with the same helper the implementation uses, baking the timezone bug into both sides; the workflow's `paths` filter omits the very files the guarded behavior depends on; the suite mocks away the component whose constraint is under test. The failure mode is asymmetric — these checks can never go red — so nobody notices they are decorative.

channel#7 smoke tests — skip instead of fail when a precondition is unmet, so absent coverage reads as passing coverage

coachflow#9 apps/api/scripts/stripe-billing-probe.ts — a usage_type=metered price satisfies active/monthly/AUD/amount and is reported ready though the app creates flat subscriptions

A probe that still exits 0 fails the build. classes.implementer_question: Write the one sentence this probe licenses you to say, then name the assertion line that would fail if that sentence were false. Specifically: does the contract probe bind its assertion to the identity of the request under test, or merely to a token that also occurs elsewhere in the same file — and what single-line mutation of production code leaves it green?

classes.title: The condition is checked by a prior SELECT while the write matches on primary key alone
classes.mechanism: Authorization scope, a cap, a time bound, a status, or a policy snapshot is verified by a read before the lock or transaction opens (or held in application memory), and the mutation then matches by bare id. Nothing in the write predicate restates the condition, so any concurrent commit or elapsed wall-clock time between read and write is undetectable — the write still succeeds and persists a decision derived from state that no longer holds. Sub-shapes: a serializable transaction is trusted to protect a condition it only READS (Postgres SSI aborts on dangerous cycles, not one-way rw-dependencies, so two transactions writing disjoint rows both commit); a callback closes over an entity fetched before the transaction; a compare-and-swap omits the very column the selection was based on; and in multi-tenant code the tenant predicate is established by a scoped findFirst and then dropped from `where: { id }`, which is correct until the reference is stale or cross-tenant.

classes.title: Several carriers hold 'who is signed in' and none is authoritative
classes.mechanism: Browser session identity lives simultaneously in an httpOnly cookie (browser-wide, server-written), sessionStorage (tab-local), React state (component-local), a URL token, and a cached role — written by several independent actors: a background cookie probe, an explicit sign-in, an OAuth callback, another tab, a guest-to-user migration. No writer carries a generation token or asserts the SUBJECT of what it is persisting, so last-writer-wins mixes accounts. Compounding shapes: resolution is written `if (token) { validateOrThrow } else { session }`, so a stale URL token destroys a valid session; a lifecycle leg is missing per carrier (token accepted but never bound to its subject or checked for expiry, a failed verify rewriting the key with a fresh TTL, clearCookie omitting the attributes used at set time); and hardening added to one frontend's client is absent from the sibling app that reimplemented the same protocol.

It contains no model of multiple browser-side carriers, cross-tab propagation, carrier precedence, or already-mounted component state, so even a reader who opened it would find nothing that fires.

classes.title: An effect that must happen once is guarded by a read, not by a claim
classes.mechanism: An invariant of the form 'at most one X' — one open checkout attempt, one credit per cancellation, one completed upload, one refund, one trial subscription, one QR token — is enforced by read-then-act with nothing that makes exactly one caller the winner: no unique index, no conditional update, no SET NX with an owner token, no GETDEL. Two concurrent callers both pass the check and both perform the effect. The dual failure is a mis-chosen identity rather than a missing one: too fine (a per-attempt random idempotency key, so a retry after a lost response moves money twice) or too coarse (a key derived from a value that does not change per logical event, so a legitimately-needed second send is suppressed). Related: a lock released by bare `del(key)` with no ownership token, and two writers to the same resource computing different lock keys.

classes.title: The predecessor generation still exists, still wins, or still cannot satisfy the new rule
classes.mechanism: A change introduces a new generation — a new canonical column, a new cookie scope, a rotated token, a new hostname, a stricter DTO, a freshly installed unit — while the previous generation's artifacts and rows persist and nobody enumerated them. Two directions: the old artifact silently WINS, because lookup and precedence favour whatever already exists (a surviving systemd drop-in carrying the revoked token, an older host-only cookie sent first, a hand-written checklist that replaces rather than dual-accepts an origin so the interim window is broken); or existing rows silently CANNOT satisfy the new constraint, because the migration added the column without backfilling, the validator rejects data shapes still in the database, or a gate is enforced before any actor has a write path to satisfy it. The inventory is drawn from memory rather than enumerated, and externally-owned registrations (Stripe webhook endpoints, OAuth redirect URIs, DNS, Vercel domains) are the entries most reliably forgotten.

classes.title: Each side of a boundary re-encodes the contract; nothing verifies the wire
classes.mechanism: Two sides of an interface independently encode the same rule or shape, and nothing joins them, so the divergence is invisible at build time. The client computes whether an action is available while the server enforces its own version — the client's copy is always simpler (status-only, ignoring expiry, eligibility, DST, falsy-vs-absent), producing buttons that always 4xx, limits that pass client validation and fail on upload, orderings that disagree between screens. The same mechanism inverts at the validator: class-validator's @IsOptional() skips BOTH undefined and null while the service branches on `!== undefined`, so an explicit JSON null passes the DTO and reaches a non-null sink (`new Date(null)` writing 1970 over a real date). And at the response boundary, `await res.json() as T` asserts a shape nothing verified, while client DTOs declare fields the server never sends and an SDK is called with the wrong verb because the contract was read from memory.

classes.title: A vendor or framework behavior is taken from expectation rather than from its docs, types, or a probe
classes.mechanism: Code maps a value or behavior produced by an external system onto exactly one internal meaning, when the producer emits it for several causes or composes it differently than assumed. Vendor values: window.open with 'noopener' returns null BY DESIGN and is read as 'popup blocked'; Charge.refunds is absent unless expanded so refunds never confirm; embedded lists are consumed via `.data` without honouring has_more while the cumulative total is still applied; at-least-once unordered webhook delivery is applied verbatim so a stale event overwrites newer state; a $0 trial invoice.paid is counted as revenue. Framework composition: Next's basePath AND the SDK each prepend the prefix so the ingest route 404s; vercel.json rewrites are written as if they ran before middleware; @OnEvent defaults to suppressErrors and emit() does not await, so a documented 'listener failure rolls back the transaction' contract does not exist; request-scoped DI is used where no request context exists; a component branches during render on localStorage or the local clock, so SSR and hydration disagree.

classes.title: The scrubber is enumerated by hand while the egress surface is defined by the vendor or the browser
classes.mechanism: What may leave the system is decided by a hand-written denylist of key names and a couple of value regexes, or by a single before-send hook, while the actual egress surface is defined elsewhere — by the vendor's payload schema, by the set of transports the SDK can open, or by the browser's degraded behaviour. Each review round names one more carrier the list forgot (auth headers, cookies, forwarded-IP headers, token/code/state query keys, PII-named keys, tuple/object query shapes, double-encoded nested URLs, DOM aria-label text, a recipient address travelling under `to`, an email used as `entityId`), and the fix adds exactly that one name. In parallel, the hook that demonstrably works is simply not on the path the data takes: Session Replay uploads its own network/URL stream, autocapture fires before any before_send and ships clicked-element text, a shallow spread clones sub-objects the field walk never revisits, and a form with JavaScript disabled degrades to a native GET that puts every entered field into the URL, browser history, Referer and access logs.

classes.title: CI/CD safety properties are hand-declared topology, each narrower or looser than reality
classes.mechanism: The pipeline's guarantees — this ran after tests, this commit was verified, this secret is visible only here, this host is who we think it is — are expressed as hand-maintained declarations that are each narrower or looser than the build's real input set. workflow_run triggers make a deploy a descendant of an image-only workflow that runs no lint/type-check/tests, so deploy and green CI can refer to different commits; a must-always-run step (migrations) is a `needs:` dependent of a best-effort or externally-probing job, so new code runs on the old schema exactly when it matters; path filters and turbo `env` lists omit real build inputs so a cached artifact ships the wrong value; a Dockerfile COPY set misses the base tsconfig. The same hand-declaration failure covers credentials: the whole production env file is attached to a container needing one variable, the registry user comes from github.actor while the token is a specific PAT, SSH steps carry the env file with no host fingerprint, preflight validates two of five secrets so failures land after remote side effects, and dispatch inputs and ExecStart read-backs are interpolated straight into shell strings and logs.

classes.title: Focus, live regions, and control state are carried by DOM identity that a swap or a wrapper silently drops
classes.mechanism: The elements assistive technology depends on are held by node identity and by prop forwarding, and both are destroyed silently. An async state machine swaps whole subtrees, so the retry button that had focus unmounts and focus falls to document.body; a live region is mounted already populated (never announced) or removed and recreated between phases; the settled error shell carries no role=status; a modal declares itself a dialog but never traps focus or inerts the page; outline-none ships with no focus-visible replacement. In parallel a shared adapter renders a control but forwards only the props it was authored for, dropping state the underlying library owns (field.disabled, field.ref), the linkage between the control and the ids the wrapper itself generates (aria-describedby, htmlFor), and the localization of its ARIA strings. Nothing throws and it looks correct, so it is invisible to snapshot tests and sighted mouse QA — and it recurs component-by-component because each fix is applied to one component rather than to a shared phase wrapper.

classes.title: Prose promoted to source of truth states an invariant nothing re-validates
classes.mechanism: A document is designated authoritative — business-knowledge docs, DESIGN.md, a technical-design spec, a deploy runbook, a design handoff — and states an invariant, a maturity level ('proven', 'fixed in PR #N'), an API shape, or a route name that no code enforces, that the same document contradicts elsewhere, or that would not compile if implemented as written. Nothing re-validates prose against the tree, so the claim is consumed by later audits, agents, and implementers as evidence the work is done, converting a live defect into an invisible one. The tell is recurrence: the same document is re-flagged round after round because each fix edits wording rather than code. The same mechanism produces specs that define two route names for one operation, letting client, controller and fixtures each pick a different URL.

classes.title: A decision is made from state that is still loading, transiently null, or cached stale
classes.mechanism: A value is consumed at a lifecycle moment when it is not yet (or no longer) authoritative, and nothing revises the decision when it settles. Telemetry identity is established on one lifecycle while events emit on an earlier one, so the initial pageview is ungrouped, a transient `user: null` during /auth/me resets identity on every hard refresh, and the tenant tag survives into the next workspace because the clearing branch exists only for full logout. On the client, a modal seeds local state in an effect whose dependency list deliberately excludes the query result (to avoid clobbering user edits), or latches on a value computed before the query resolved, or from a raw list the render layer later filters differently — so on a slow load the seed is derived from empty input and the recovery behaviour the feature exists to provide never fires. A value captured at render (`now`, a cached role) is likewise never recomputed, so an action stays disabled after its time passes and entitlement UI disagrees with the server's current authorization answer.

classes.title: A call site uses the host default or a raw literal instead of the domain's designated authority
classes.mechanism: The domain designates an authority for a value — the tenant's salon timezone, the design foundation's tokens — but individual call sites reach for the ambient or raw equivalent instead. Time: `format(date,'yyyy-MM-dd')`, `getHours()`, `setHours(0,0,0,0)`, server-side `parseISO`, `startOfDay/endOfDay` are each locally correct in the developer's timezone and in a UTC CI runner, so drift manifests only for cross-timezone staff or a non-UTC host — shifted labels, availability queried over the wrong day bounds, a slot booked at a different instant than the one displayed. Design: literal hex/rgba, arbitrary rounded-[32px] and shadow values, non-canonical tracking for a composition-locked pattern, or a hand-built card duplicating the shared shell. Neither kind propagates: a later palette, radius, per-tenant theme, or timezone-handling change silently skips these surfaces, and each new screen widens the divergence.
exemplars: luxebook#59 apps/api/src/modules/scheduling/availability.service.ts — dayStart/dayEnd moved to tenant-local while getBlocksForDate still uses server-local startOfDay/endOfDay, so blocked times return as available

luxebook#79 packages/ui/src/components/booking-slot-picker.tsx — slot labels built from getHours()/getMinutes() in browser TZ, so a 17:00 salon slot can display as 09:00 while the backend books the original instant
luxebook#79 apps/admin/src/lib/hooks/use-booking-reschedule.ts — dateIso derived with browser-local format(), so the modal fetches the wrong calendar day's inventory
luxebook#109 tenant-unavailable-view.tsx — hand-built card with raw bg-white and inline rgba() invents a palette value outside the foundation, so theme/token changes never reach this state
luxebook#109 tenant-unavailable-view.tsx — font-semibold tracking-[0.24em] diverges from the composition-locked DESIGN.md eyebrow (font-medium tracking-[0.22em])
nutribuddy — hardcoded colors on new surfaces instead of the shared tokens
classes.why_it_did_not_fire: trigger keywords too narrow — two separate rules each cover one instance of the same mechanism, and both are keyed on a narrow token list: server-local-trap on `parseISO`/`startOfDay`/`getHours`/'scheduling', design-system-drift on 'Tailwind class change, breakpoint stack, native input restyling'. A plain `format()` in an admin hook and an `rgba()` literal in a new error-state component match neither list, so a diff that drifts from BOTH authorities loads neither rule.
classes.gate_idea: ESLint no-restricted-syntax banning date-fns `format|startOfDay|endOfDay|parseISO` and `Date.prototype.getHours|getMinutes|getDay` inside scheduling/booking modules and calendar UI unless the call is date-fns-tz (formatInTimeZone/toZonedTime) or carries an allowlist comment; plus a CI matrix running unit and E2E twice (TZ=UTC and TZ=Asia/Hong_Kong) and requiring byte-identical results. In parallel, an AST/regex lint over apps/*/src/**/*.tsx failing on #rrggbb, rgb(/rgba( literals, rounded-[, shadow-[, tracking-[, and non-token palette utilities outside an explicit allowlist — resolving tracking/weight pairs for eyebrow/heading classes against values extracted from DESIGN.md so drift from a composition-locked pattern fails; a Tailwind-config-driven test that every utility used exists in the tenant-token preset; and a CI check that any PR adding a new route- or state-level component also references a file under design/.
classes.implementer_question: For each new date computation in this diff, name the timezone it is evaluated in and show the tenant timezone being passed explicitly; for each color, radius, shadow and tracking value, name the DESIGN.md token alias it resolves to. Did you run this suite under both TZ=UTC and TZ=Asia/Hong_Kong, and does any value in the diff come from the host default or a raw literal rather than the designated authority?
